method.title: How this value is estimated:
method.text: the simulation adds salary and variable average, counts months with at least 15 worked days, applies 1/12 avos, separates installments, and estimates 13th-salary legal deductions when available.
method.sourceNote: Brazilian legal sources checked on {accessDate}; INSS {inssYear} and IRRF {irrfYear} tables. Educational estimate only; official payroll, eSocial, collective agreements, and professional review prevail.

howToCalculate.title: How Brazilian 13th salary is calculated
howToCalculate.p1: The calculation starts with base remuneration, made from monthly salary and the variable-pay average entered by the user.
howToCalculate.p2: The tool multiplies that base by the year avos and divides by 12. A month is counted only when it has at least 15 worked days in the informed period.

avos.title: What avos mean for 13th salary
avos.text: Avos are 1/12 fractions of Brazilian 13th salary. An employee with 12 avos receives a full gross 13th; someone hired during the year receives the proportion for months that reached 15 days.

installments.title: First and second 13th salary installments
installments.p1: The first installment is shown as an estimated 50% advance on gross 13th salary.
installments.p2: The second installment starts from the remaining gross 13th salary and concentrates estimated deductions when INSS/IRRF is enabled.

proportional.title: Proportional 13th salary for employees hired during the year
proportional.text: Enter the hire date and reference date to see which months count. Months with fewer than 15 worked days stay out of the avos count.

deductions.title: How INSS and IRRF apply to 13th salary
deductions.p1: When the year is 2026, the calculator estimates INSS on 13th salary as a separate base and then estimates IRRF with dependents, alimony, and simplified discount.
deductions.p2: For other years, or when legal deductions are disabled, the result remains gross and manual fields can adjust deductions or additions.

limitations.title: Calculator limits
limitations.text: The official value can change because of actual variable averages, absences and leaves, multiple jobs, INSS ceiling use, court-ordered alimony, payroll rubrics, collective agreements, and professional interpretation.

q1.question: How do I calculate proportional Brazilian 13th salary?
q1.answer: Count the months in the year with at least 15 worked days, multiply base remuneration by those avos, and divide by 12.

q2.question: Does a month with fewer than 15 days count?
q2.answer: No. In this estimate, a month creates one avo only when the employment relationship reaches 15 or more days in that month.

q3.question: When are the first and second installments paid?
q3.answer: The tool shows the first installment as an estimated advance and the second as the balance before deductions. Actual dates depend on payroll and applicable rules.

q4.question: Is 13th salary INSS separate from monthly salary?
q4.answer: The estimate treats 13th salary as a separate INSS and IRRF base using 2026 tables, matching the operational rule planned for this calculator.

q5.question: Does the calculator show the exact net amount?
q5.answer: No. It estimates from the entered data and 2026 tables. Official payroll can change due to averages, rubrics, advances, INSS ceiling, alimony, and collective agreements.

q6.question: How do commissions, overtime, or variable salary enter?
q6.answer: Use the monthly variable-pay average field for a habitual average. The calculator does not infer monthly commission or overtime history.
